skills.name: accio
skills.description: Search code with accio.cmd instead of grep, rg or find.
skills.html:
Accio

Below, accio is ./community/tools/accio.cmd in the monorepo and ./tools/accio.cmd in a community checkout.

Pick by what you hold. Batch independent names or queries with the same command and options in one invocation:

  • A change to make, described in words (a bug to fix, a feature to add; not a question about the code): accio context 'the change as written, then the identifiers the task names' --bodies 5 first: candidate locations, with source and related uses and tests where available; then the lookups below only for what it did not show.
  • A name from the task (class, function, member): accio symbol Name --source-lines prints the declaration with its body (a long function's first 30 lines; all for the whole); several at once: accio symbol A B --source-lines. A short file comes whole; otherwise the body names the file's imports and the same-file declarations it uses.
  • Text the code contains: accio locate 'text' --scope dir/; a small answer shows the lines around each hit; several texts in one call: accio locate 'a' 'b'. Alternatives: accio locate 'a|b' --mode regex, never a\|b.
  • A file name you know only in part: accio files 'Service*'; quote globs. A file whose path you know needs no lookup: accio locate 'text' --scope path/File.kt shows its lines around each hit.
  • A behaviour, with no name, text or path to go on: accio locate 'how does X happen' --mode semantic, a full question; ranked leads, inspect the relevant one and stop. To plan an edit at a known place: accio context 'change X' --scope dir/.
  • Changing or deleting a declaration: accio references Name for every use, labelled; accio implementations Type for subtypes. Structural leads, not compiler proofs.

An answer is bounded: read it whole, never through head. Trust an exact or structural, complete answer within its reported coverage and stop; narrow with --scope rather than a second search. heuristic or unknown: a ranked lead, not an answer. partial: narrow --scope or raise --limit. match=similar: the name matched ignoring case. At zero hits or unavailable, the note and separate alternatives explain the miss; alternatives are not matches in the requested scope. An error is not evidence of absence.

The rest: accio trace Name and accio impact Name walk the call graph, accio tests Name the tests that reach it, accio unused --scope dir/ lists dead-code candidates; accio <command> --help has every flag. --scope takes directories, quoted globs ('*.kt', '!**/generated/**') or files, repeatable; --no-tests drops tests; --project <dir> a dependency's sources, git or not; --format json for parsing.

In this repository

  • accio indexes the files that git tracks, dot-directories such as .agents/ included.
  • A --scope that names a git-ignored file or a directory under it is read from the working tree, for example --scope out/air/. A directory outside the repository is read from disk.
  • --mode regex has no look-around. Use rg.cmd --pcre2 for it.
  • For dead code, use accio unused with the duplicate-and-dead-code skill.

skills.name: actions
skills.description: Implement or change IntelliJ `AnAction` actions and registrations.
skills.html:
Actions

Documentation

  • Action System - Architecture and usage of the action system

Best Practices

  • NEVER instantiate Presentation in action constructors - Use no-argument constructors
  • Use AnActionEvent#getCoroutineScope for launching suspending computations - actionPerformed runs synchronously with event invocation and may freeze the IDE.
  • Follow the convention:
    1. Set the id attribute for the action in plugin.xml
    2. Optionally set the icon attribute if an icon is needed
    3. Set text and description in the message bundle (e.g., GitBundle.properties):
    • action.<action-id>.text=Translated Action Text
    • action.<action-id>.description=Translated Action Description

Good example:

Kotlin:

class MyAction : AnAction()

plugin.xml:

<action id="My.Action.Id"
        class="my.package.MyAction"
        icon="my.package.MyIcons.ICON"/>

skills.name: bazel-test-migration
skills.description: Migrate IntelliJ JPS module tests to Bazel; debug Bazel-only failures.
skills.html:
Bazel Test Migration

Keep existing test behavior unless a failure proves that the test depends on an invalid environment assumption.

Establish the Baseline

  • Use earlier migration commits as references, not patches to apply unchanged.
  • Identify the module that contains the tests. From Ultimate, use @community//... for Community targets. From standalone Community, use //....
  • Record known failures and the user's exclusions from the task. Do not fix unrelated failures or silently remove them from the run.
  • Use existing CI results or an initial target run to establish the failures.

During migration, run the Bazel target directly if bt refuses a module that is not yet marked as migrated.

Configure the Target

Follow the module dependencies skill for registration and generation.

  • Use scope="RUNTIME" for plugins needed only for runtime loading, descriptors, extensions, or resources. Do not add them as TEST merely because tests need them.
  • Keep APIs required to compile test sources in the appropriate compile or TEST scope.
  • Load the owning plugin or wrapper when its descriptor is required. Do not manually register production extensions in test setup.
  • Fix a production descriptor only if its dependency is also wrong in production. An incomplete test product usually needs a test module dependency.
  • Keep custom jps_test declarations outside generated sections. Preserve the existing runtime_deps, tags, timeout, env, jvm_flags, and data.

Do not patch missing jars or descriptors into runfiles with copy_file.

Resolve Test Inputs

Use all three parts of the test data contract:

  1. Declare the required files in a filegroup, or reuse an existing one.
  2. Add that target to the test's data.
  3. Resolve the runtime path through an existing helper or BazelTestUtil.getFileFromBazelRuntime(BazelLabel).

Prefer a helper such as JavaTestUtil.getJavaTestDataPath() when it already supports Bazel. Keep the existing non-Bazel behavior. Check static fields, companion properties, and serialization inputs as well as fixture path overrides.

  • Keep the path returned by the runfiles resolver, including manifest-based results. Do not use toRealPath() to redirect test data back to the checkout.
  • Do not construct paths from PathManager.getHomePath(), community+, or _main under Bazel. The resolver handles repository mapping.
  • Preserve relative-path API contracts. When a fixture joins a base path to the repository root, override its absolute getTestDataPath() instead.
  • A filegroup declares files; it does not rename them. Check that the requested label path exists among the runtime inputs.
  • Treat test data and downloaded archives as read-only. Copy projects or unpack archives into a unique temporary directory before modifying them.

Read test data and writable files for examples and VFS access handling. For downloads or child builds, read external inputs and nested builds.

Debug Focused Failures

Run the failing class with fresh test results:

./bazel.cmd test --cache_test_results=no \
  --test_filter='com.example.ExampleTest' \
  @community//path/to/package:target_test

Use com.example.ExampleTest#testMethod for one method. Avoid repeated full-module runs while diagnosing a focused failure.

  • Read test.log, idea.log, and JUnit XML. Inspect the actual command, environment, and declared inputs before changing assertions.
  • Distinguish missing input or plugin wiring from behavior failures. Use failure diagnosis for common cases.
  • If a test passes alone, check shared state and project reuse. Restore settings and include relevant configuration in fixture cache identity.
  • Fix a shared helper when it owns the defect.
  • Keep broad platform or JDK fixes separate when they need independent review. A temporary test-local workaround must preserve the test's purpose and identify the follow-up.
  • Keep existing assertions and coverage. Do not add exclusions, assumptions, or disabled tests merely to make the migration green.
  • Use assumptions only for genuine environment restrictions. Declare required environment variables in the target instead of relying on the developer's shell.

Verify the Complete Target

Remove diagnostic selectors and run the exact target without a test filter:

./bazel.cmd test --cache_test_results=no @community//path/to/package:target_test
  • Confirm that tests actually ran. A selected method can pass even when normal discovery misses its class.
  • Check the test library and discovery roots before changing placement. Adding a dependency does not guarantee that its tests are discovered.
  • Separate framework tests into a dedicated module or Bazel package when their current placement mixes framework code and executable tests.
  • Do not use a growing class whitelist to compensate for incorrect placement. Keep the new module with its natural owner.
  • Prefer sandbox = True once inputs and writable locations are declared. Preserve an existing sandbox; document any remaining exception.
  • Check affected JPS or IDE runs when changing shared helpers. Check relevant CI platforms because local success does not prove portable path handling.

See discovery and sandbox checks for details.

Complete the Switch

  • Select complete modules through the target tags and CI configuration. Do not migrate only the convenient classes in a module.
  • For a CI rollout, compare actual test coverage before removing the JPS run. Follow CI coverage comparison.
  • Check CI and Safe-Push selection separately. Update their target lists or selectors within the requested scope; keep JPS coverage for modules not yet migrated.
  • Add the module to the migrated-module list only after verification and replacement coverage are established.
  • The list makes tests.cmd refuse migrated modules. Do not assume it configures every CI build or automatically removes every JPS invocation.
  • Report the focused and complete runs, known failures, and any unverified CI coverage. Do not describe a run as green when known failures remain.

Keep test data resolution changes separate from configuration changes when that makes review easier.

skills.name: code-style
skills.description: Apply IntelliJ Kotlin and Java code style when writing or reviewing.
skills.html:
Code Style

Follow the IntelliJ Coding Guidelines with these IntelliJ-specific rules.

Language

  • Use Kotlin for new files unless the user explicitly requests Java.
  • Keep existing Java files in Java unless the task requires a language conversion.
  • Before writing or reviewing Java, read Modern Java.
  • Use idiomatic Kotlin: extension functions, data classes, null safety
  • Mark experimental APIs with @ApiStatus.Experimental
  • Build scripts Kotlin style: Follow community/platform/build-scripts/kotlin-style-recommendations.md for build-scripts code.

Sealed hierarchies

  • Before you list several subtypes in a when branch, an is check, or a catch, open the declaration of the type.
  • If a common supertype covers exactly those subtypes, use the supertype. It stays correct when someone adds a new subtype.
  • Check the value of a sealed type or an enum with an exhaustive when. Do not use an is check, an as? cast, an == comparison, or else. In Eel and IJent code, this is a rule, also for a private type. See community/platform/eel/docs/api/exhaustive-when.md.

Formatting

  • Read every applicable .editorconfig before you review or change formatting.
  • Use the effective .editorconfig value for each setting. If no file defines a setting, use these defaults:
    • Indentation: 2 spaces (4 for Go files)
    • Line length: 140 characters max
    • Braces: else, catch, and finally on new lines
  • In /rustrover directory, except /rustrover/build, you must always use standard Kotlin formatting rules with 4 spaces indentation.

Threading annotations

  • When you add @RequiresEdt, @RequiresBackgroundThread, @RequiresReadLock, @RequiresWriteLock, or @RequiresReadLockAbsence, do not pass generateAssertion. Keep the default value unless the user explicitly requests a different one.
  • Never write generateAssertion = false /* IJPL-115548 */. It is a legacy mass-migration marker. Do not copy it from existing code.
  • Set generateAssertion = false only when the user explicitly requests it, or when the runtime assertion is known to fail. State the reason in a comment.

Error handling

  • In a catch block for Throwable or Exception, call com.intellij.diagnostic.rethrowControlFlowException(e) first. It rethrows a control flow exception, such as CancellationException. A control flow exception must never reach the log.
  • Do not catch or rethrow CancellationException explicitly, and do not test the exception type by hand.
  • In Java, static-import com.intellij.diagnostic.ControlFlowExceptionsKt.rethrowControlFlowException.
  • Do not use the deprecated com.intellij.openapi.diagnostic.rethrowControlFlowException.
try {
  doWork()
}
catch (e: Throwable) {
  rethrowControlFlowException(e)
  LOG.error(e)
}

skills.name: commits
skills.description: Read before each commit, amend or reword: the subject SafePush accepts and the body.
skills.html:
Commits

Scope

  • One commit does one thing. Do not mix a cleanup or a refactoring into a behavioral change. When unsure, split.
  • Check the scope with git status --short and git diff --stat. Read the full diff only for changes you did not make in this session.

Message

IDEA-12345 <subject>              # a change with a ticket: the id, then one sentence
<label> <subsystem>: <subject>    # a change with no ticket
  • A behavioral change needs a YouTrack ticket. If you are unsure whether it is behavioral, it is.
  • Write <subject> as an imperative sentence. The body stays declarative.
  • With a ticket, the subject is the id and one sentence that says what the change does or decides. Do not add a label or a subsystem: the id already names the area. IDEA-12345 skip a generated file in the inspection, not IDEA-12345 the inspection skips a generated file or IDEA-12345 fix inspections: generated files. A test, a docs, or a cleanup commit of a ticket takes the same form; the body says that it is a test or a docs change. A module AGENTS.md can require a subsystem, and its rule wins.
  • With no ticket, the label is one of tests, cleanup, refactor, docs, format, style, setup, misc.
  • With a Branch Deck prefix, the subject is (branch) <the form above>. Branch Deck removes the prefix at the push, so the rest must pass SafePush alone.
  • Do not use Conventional Commits (fix(scope): …).
  • Put a requested suffix such as IJ-MR-100 in its own last paragraph.

Body

Write a body unless the change is mechanical (a typo, an import, a format pass). Tests and cleanups need one too.

  • The diff shows what changed. The body says why.
  • The first paragraph is the lead: the new state and its cause, in 1-3 sentences.
  • Then one paragraph for each decision that a reader could question: what you chose, what you did not choose, and why. Skip an obvious decision and a detail that the diff shows. Write code names in backticks.
  • Do not report a test run, a build, or a test that fails also without the change. A commit in master compiles and passes its tests. Give a measurement that caused the change in the lead or in its decision.
  • Do not name a stage, a session or a step of a plan. A reader of the history does not have the plan. Say the remaining work in words.

Passing the message

In a POSIX shell, use a quoted heredoc:

git commit -F - <<'EOF'
IDEA-12345 concise subject

Why the change was made and what was decided.
EOF

In PowerShell, pass one -m per paragraph, also with --amend. Do not pipe a here-string into -F -. Windows PowerShell adds a BOM to the subject, and SafePush rejects it.

git commit -m "IDEA-12345 concise subject" -m "Why the change was made and what was decided." -m "IJ-MR-100"

Do not write the message to a file outside the workspace, such as /tmp: that asks for a filesystem approval and leaves a plaintext draft behind. If you need a file, give it a name unique to your session under the gitignored out/, such as out/commit-message-<session>.txt. Several sessions share one working copy, and a peer can overwrite a shared file name between your write and your commit.

Examples

IJAI-3334 name the step of the published-surface wait in the editor service test and dump the state

The test failed once on TeamCity with no log line in its 10 s window, and 208 local runs did not reproduce it.
The helper now waits for the subscription and then for the apply, under one deadline, and a failure adds the
state of the test backend and a coroutine dump. No product code changes.

A change with no ticket, with a Branch Deck prefix:

(dev-dist-cache) setup build: write the pinned Qodana build date into the dev dist launch model

QD-16701 added -Dqodana.build.date=<yyyyMMddHHmm> to the qodana command of the production product-info.json.
`computeProductLaunchModel` gave no date to `QodanaProductProperties`, so the dev dist model had no such argument.
`DistProductLaunchModelTest` compares both files byte for byte, and it failed.

The model now states the token @@build_date@@, next to @@build_number@@. product-files replaces it with the date
of --build-date-seconds, which the action already receives. A test exclusion would hide a real difference
of the dev dist qodana command, so the tool writes the argument as production does.

Other cases, such as isolated commits and misc triage: 2_Commits.md. To push, use the safe-push skill.

Windows PowerShell adds a BOM to the subject, and SafePush rejects it. powershell git commit -m "IDEA-12345 concise subject" -m "Why the change was made and what was decided." -m "IJ-MR-100" Do not write the message to a file outside the workspace, such as /tmp : that asks for a filesystem approval and leaves a plaintext draft behind. If you need a file, give it a name unique to your session under the gitignored out/ , such as out/commit-message-<session .txt . Several sessions share one working copy, and a peer can overwrite a shared file name between your write and your commit. Examples text IJAI-3334 name the step of the published-surface wait in the editor service test and dump the state The test failed once on TeamCity with no log line in its 10 s window, and 208 local runs did not reproduce it. The helper now waits for the subscription and then for the apply, under one deadline, and a failure adds the state of the test backend and a coroutine dump. No product code changes. A change with no ticket, with a Branch Deck prefix: text (dev-dist-cache) setup build: write the pinned Qodana build date into the dev dist launch model QD-16701 added -Dqodana.build.date=<yyyyMMddHHmm to the qodana command of the production product-info.json. computeProductLaunchModel gave no date to QodanaProductProperties , so the dev dist model had no such argument. DistProductLaunchModelTest compares both files byte for byte, and it failed. The model now states the token @@build date@@, next to @@build number@@. product-files replaces it with the date of --build-date-seconds, which the action already receives. A test exclusion would hide a real difference of the dev dist qodana command, so the tool writes the argument as production does. Other cases, such as isolated commits and misc triage: 2 Commits.md. To push, use the safe-push skill.

skills.name: compare-python-typecheckers
skills.description: Compare Python type inference with ty, pyrefly, and basedpyright.
skills.html:
Compare Python type checkers

Run it

scripts/compare_typecheckers.py runs ty, pyrefly, basedpyright, mypy and zuban through uvx: no install, and the first run needs the network. It prints a Markdown report: a summary table (command, exit code, verdict and time for each tool), then the raw output of each tool.

uv run ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/compare_typecheckers.py path/to/test.py
uv run ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/compare_typecheckers.py -c '<code>' --tools ty,mypy -o /tmp/report.md

Flags: -c/--code (inline snippet), -t/--tools ty,mypy,… (subset), -o/--output (write to file), --timeout (per-checker seconds, default 180). The script exits 0 whenever it produced a report — findings live in the report, not the exit code.

Reading the result

  • basedpyright is pyright-based and also emits extra diagnostics such as reportUnusedCallResult.
  • The checkers track their latest releases through uvx, so behaviour can shift over time — record the date when capturing results in a YouTrack issue or test.
  • For a run by hand, take the command of a checker from CHECKERS in the script.

skills.name: conda-env-tests
skills.description: Bump the Miniconda version of the Python conda env tests.
skills.html:
Conda env tests

Where the pin lives

One file holds every conda pin:

community/python/python-test-env/common/src/com/intellij/python/test/env/common/PredefinedPyEnvironments.kt

CONDA is the default. @PyEnvTestCaseWithConda and LocalCondaRule use it. A bump moves CONDA only. No test uses CONDA_24 or CONDA_25.

The provider builds the download URL from the pin. It verifies no checksum, and it accepts the terms of service of the Anaconda channels:

community/python/python-test-env/conda/src/com/intellij/python/test/env/conda/CondaPyEnvironmentProvider.kt

ShortenPathTest holds the literal Miniconda3-py312_24.9.2-0-MacOSX-arm64 as sample text. Do not change it.

The version token

A pin is the installer version token, not a plain conda version. The shape is py<python>_<conda>-<build>, for example py312_26.7.1-1.

The provider expands the token into one of these names:

  • Miniconda3-<token>-Windows-x86_64.exe
  • Miniconda3-<token>-Windows-arm64.exe
  • Miniconda3-<token>-Linux-x86_64.sh
  • Miniconda3-<token>-Linux-aarch64.sh
  • Miniconda3-<token>-MacOSX-arm64.sh

How to pick a new pin

  1. Open https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/.
  2. Take the highest version. Do not use Miniconda3-latest-*. The cache key holds the token, so a floating name breaks reproducibility.
  3. Check that each name above exists for that token. Anaconda drops a platform from time to time.
  4. Keep the py<python> prefix of the entry unless you have a reason to change it. The prefix only sets the Python of the base install. Each test environment gets its own Python from the spec.

The download cache

The tests cache in ~/.cache/intellij-python-test-env/:

  • downloads/ holds the installer.
  • conda/Miniconda3-<token>-<os>-<arch>/ holds the install.

A bump downloads the installer again. It leaves the old installer and the old directory on disk. Delete them by hand when you need the space.

Tests to run

The tests need the network.

Module Class
intellij.python.test.env.junit5 com.intellij.python.test.env.junit5.conda.showcase.PyEnvWithCondaShowCaseTest
intellij.python.community.impl.conda.tests com.intellij.python.junit5Tests.env.tests.conda.CondaSdkCreatorTest

Not this skill

community/python/python-sdk/backend/resources/sdks.json lists the Miniconda builds that the product offers to a user. The run configuration PyCharm Update Sdks generates it. The provider does not read it.

skills.name: content-module
skills.description: Create, convert or extract an IntelliJ plugin content module.
skills.html:
Plugin content modules

Use this skill for one of three tasks:

  • Create a new content module.
  • Convert an existing module that the build merges into the plugin descriptor module.
  • Extract an optional dependency of a module into a new content module.

This skill does not apply to a module in the core plugin (com.intellij). The core plugin registers its content modules in a module set. See the Product DSL.

The rules live in the docs. Read them, and do not restate them in code or in other skills:

  • Creating a plugin content module: the descriptor, the visibility, the registration and the compatibility.
  • Modules in project sources: the source roots and the package prefix.
  • Plugin Model v1 and v2: the loading rules.
  • Plugin directory structure: the layout of a split mode plugin.

Other skills cover nearby tasks:

  • To change .iml dependencies, use the module-dependencies skill.
  • To query which plugins and products include a module, use the plugin-model-analyzer skill.
  • To split a plugin for split mode, use the remote-dev skill.

Create a new content module

Create the module with the CLI. Do not write an .iml or a modules.xml entry by hand:

bun build/jps-module.mjs create <module-dir>/<module-name>.iml [--kind empty|shared|frontend|backend] [--plugin <plugin.xml>]

The command does these steps:

  • It writes the .iml in the canonical form. The src root gets the root package com.<module-name> as its package prefix.
  • The kinds shared, frontend and backend copy the template plugins/.remdev/remDevFeatureSample.<kind>. Only the ultimate checkout has the template.
  • It registers the module in .idea/modules.xml, and also in community/.idea/modules.xml for a community module.
  • It adds <module name="..."/> to the <content> of the plugin descriptor, with the loading rule of the kind.

Rules for the arguments:

  • The name of the .iml file is the module name. Its directory is the module directory. Each module needs a directory of its own.
  • The default kind is the suffix of the module name: .shared, .frontend or .backend. Any other name gets empty.
  • Create the .shared module first. A frontend or backend module refuses to start without it.
  • For shared, frontend and backend, the default plugin descriptor is ../resources/META-INF/plugin.xml beside the module directory. Pass --plugin for another descriptor.
  • An empty module goes into a plugin only with --plugin, because a test or helper module is not a content module.
  • An empty module gets no loading rule, so it is optional. Add loading="required" to its entry when the plugin needs it.

The templates declare kotlin-stdlib and the .shared module with scope="RUNTIME". When the code of the module uses them at compile time, change the scope with the module-dependencies skill. Without kotlin-stdlib at compile time, Kotlin fails with Cannot access built-in declaration 'kotlin.Any' on almost every line.

Then do the common steps.

The package prefix keeps the source tree flat. The file com/intellij/foo/bar/Baz.kt of the module intellij.foo goes to src/bar/Baz.kt. A package outside com.<module-name> fails IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest.

Convert an existing module

Use this when a JPS module already exists and the build merges it into the plugin descriptor module. The goal is to register it as a content module and keep the same behavior at runtime.

1. Find how the plugin includes the module now

Search for the module name and for the file name of its XML descriptor. Record the current form. It sets the loading rule in step 3.

Current form Loading rule
<depends optional="true" config-file="..."> in plugin.xml optional (the default, no attribute)
<xi:include> with an empty <xi:fallback/> optional
<xi:include> without a fallback required
A JAR in a subdirectory of lib, so the IDE process does not load it on-demand
The JAR is in the plugin, but the module has no XML of its own required

Also find where the build layout names the module:

  • pluginAuto(...) moduleNames or spec.withModule(...) in CommunityRepositoryModules.kt or UltimateRepositoryModules.kt.
  • An automatic merge by inferModuleSources in autoLayout.kt, when the module name starts with the plugin descriptor module name.

2. Move the module descriptor

Put the descriptor at <module-dir>/resources/<module-name>.xml. Do not put it in META-INF. If the old XML is in META-INF or has a different name, move it with git mv. The docs list the tags that a module descriptor can have. Remove the package attribute. Keep a <module value="..."/> plugin alias only when the old code already declared it.

3. Register the module in the plugin descriptor

Add the module to the <content> of the plugin plugin.xml, with the loading rule from step 1. Remove the old depends or xi:include tag. Remove the module from the build layout entries that you found in step 1. The build adds a content module to the distribution automatically.

If the layout gave the JAR a custom name, update the code that uses that name. A content module goes to lib/<module-name>.jar when it is embedded, and to lib/modules/<module-name>.jar in the other cases. When the layout spec becomes empty, remove the whole pluginAuto or plugin call.

4. Keep compatibility with external plugins

Skip this step for loading="embedded". Call the get_external_usage_statistics tool for each public class. The index covers only Marketplace plugins, so an empty result does not prove safety. If there are external usages, call find_external_usages on plugin.xml to see how the external plugins depend on the plugin.

Then do the common steps.

Extract an optional dependency

Use this to make a dependency X of a host module optional: move the code that uses X into a new content module. The host module works when the new module is absent, and behaves the same when it is present.

Choose the pattern

  • Pattern A, a simple move. The code that uses X is in a few files, and the host module does not call them. Move these files to the new module.
  • Pattern B, an extension point. The core files of the host module refer to X in many places. Declare an extension point in the host module without X imports. Implement it in the new module, and replace each direct X call with a null-safe static helper.

1. Create the module

Create the module with bun build/jps-module.mjs create <module-dir>/<module-name>.iml --plugin <plugin.xml>. The kind is usually empty, which makes it optional. Add its dependencies with the module-dependencies skill: the host module and X.

2. Move the code

  • Keep the type of a moved file, Kotlin or Java. Write new code in Kotlin.
  • Move the file and change its package declaration together.
  • Keep the availability in IDEA Free mode. The host module and the new module both keep the availability of the original module. PluginsAvailableInIdeaFreeModeTest checks this.

Bazel strict deps needs a direct .iml dependency for each class that the code uses. These classes live in modules that their package names do not suggest:

Class(es) Package .iml module Bazel target
ExecutionException, GeneralCommandLine, KillableColoredProcessHandler, OSProcessHandler, ScriptRunnerUtil, Url, NetUtils com.intellij.execution.*, com.intellij.util.* intellij.platform.ide.util.io @community//platform/platform-util-io:ide-util-io
AsyncPromise, Promise org.jetbrains.concurrency intellij.platform.concurrency @community//platform/util/concurrency
AppExecutorUtil, ProcessAdapter, ProcessEvent, ProcessOutputTypes, ParametersListUtil, FileUtil, StringUtil com.intellij.util.*, com.intellij.openapi.util.* intellij.platform.util @community//platform/util
Editor com.intellij.openapi.editor intellij.platform.editor.ui @community//platform/editor-ui-api
MultipleLangCommentProvider com.intellij.psi.templateLanguages intellij.platform.lang.impl @community//platform/lang-impl

When the code calls a method whose return type comes from a third module, that module is also a direct dependency. Kotlin checks the return type at compile time.

3. Declare the extension point (Pattern B only)

Declare the extension point in the descriptor of the host module with qualifiedName:

<extensionPoints>
  <extensionPoint qualifiedName="com.intellij.<language>.<epName>"
                  interface="com.intellij.<language>.<feature>.MyFeatureHelper"
                  dynamic="true"/>
</extensionPoints>

Write the interface in the host module, without X imports. Give it @JvmStatic helpers that return a no-op result when no extension is registered:

interface MyFeatureHelper {
  fun doSomething(element: PsiElement): Boolean

  companion object {
    @JvmField
    val EP = ExtensionPointName.create<MyFeatureHelper>("com.intellij.<language>.<epName>")

    // An extension point can have several extensions. Process all of them.
    @JvmStatic fun checkSomething(element: PsiElement?): Boolean =
      element != null && EP.extensionList.any { it.doSomething(element) }
  }
}

Register the implementation in the descriptor of the new module:

<extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij">
  <<language>.<epName> implementation="com.intellij.<language>.<feature>.MyFeatureHelperImpl"/>
</extensions>

When the operations of X form a lifecycle, put them in one extension point, not one per method. When a step passes state of an X type to a later step, type the state as Any? in the interface. The implementation casts it back:

// In the host module, without X imports
interface MyLifecycleHelper {
  fun captureState(file: PsiFile): Any?
  fun applyState(file: PsiFile, state: Any?)
}

// In the new module
internal class MyLifecycleHelperImpl : MyLifecycleHelper {
  override fun captureState(file: PsiFile): Any? = getThings(file)

  override fun applyState(file: PsiFile, state: Any?) {
    @Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
    val things = state as? List<XThing> ?: emptyList()
  }
}

4. Fix the users of the removed dependency

A module that used X through the host module can break. AllProductsPackagingTest#targetValidations names it. Add the dependency to its descriptor before the <!-- region Generated dependencies --> marker, inside the same <dependencies> tag:

<dependencies>
  <module name="intellij.some.formerly.transitive.module"/>
  <!-- region Generated dependencies - run `Generate Product Layouts` to regenerate -->
  ...
  <!-- endregion -->
</dependencies>

Do not add a second <dependencies> tag. AllProductsPackagingTest#suiteValidations then reports the file as out of sync.

When another plugin uses a moved class, do these steps for that plugin:

  1. Add <module name="intellij.new.module"/> to its descriptor.
  2. Add the module to its .iml with the module-dependencies skill.
  3. Set the visibility of the new module. The docs say which level to use.

Kotlin classes are final by default. When another module subclasses a moved class or its inner class, mark both classes open. Otherwise the other module fails with cannot inherit from final class.

Then do the common steps.

Common steps

  1. Run ./build/jpsModelToBazel.cmd after an .iml change. In a community checkout, run ./build/jpsModelToBazelCommunityOnly.cmd.
  2. Run ./bazel.cmd run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool. It generates the <dependencies> of the module descriptors from the .iml files. Read each change that it makes.
  3. Run ./community/tools/bt.cmd build for the new module and for each module whose descriptor changed.
  4. Run the tests. bt refuses intellij.projectStructureTests, because its tests do not run under Bazel yet, so these tests use tests.cmd. Run the tests.cmd runs one at a time. Each run stops the ide-tests processes of a run that is still in progress.
./community/tools/bt.cmd //build/tests/smoke:all-products-packaging_test
./tests.cmd --module intellij.projectStructureTests --test com.intellij.ideaProjectStructure.fast.IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest
./tests.cmd --module intellij.projectStructureTests --test com.intellij.ideaProjectStructure.fast.PluginsAvailableInIdeaFreeModeTest

For Rider, also run ./tests.cmd --module intellij.rider.build.tests --test com.jetbrains.rider.build.RiderPackagingTest from the ultimate root. After a conversion, search for the old descriptor file name. No xi:include or config-file reference to it can remain.

Pitfalls

Pitfall Symptom Fix
A src tree that repeats the root package as directories Deep src/com/intellij/... folders Keep the package prefix of src, and move the files up
A package outside com.<module-name> IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest fails Rename the package. Do not add an entry to non-standard-root-packages.txt for a new module
A moved file with the old package declaration IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest: "packages [com.old.pkg] are found in the module" Change the package declaration with the move
An extension point with name instead of qualifiedName The extension point is not found Use qualifiedName="com.intellij.<language>.<epName>"
A skipped plugin-model-tool run The generated descriptors have stale dependencies Run ./bazel.cmd run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool
A supertype in a removed dependency Cannot access 'com.X.BaseClass' which is a supertype of 'SubClass' Kotlin needs the full supertype chain of each used type. Move the use of SubClass into the extension point implementation, and return a type without X
A template dependency with scope="RUNTIME" Cannot access built-in declaration 'kotlin.Any', or an unresolved class of the .shared module Change the scope of kotlin-stdlib or of the .shared module to compile
A class hierarchy that needs a platform dependency cannot access BaseClass: class file not found Keep the platform dependency, also without direct imports
A large move Many modules fail to compile After you move 10 or more files, build //plugins/... //contrib/...
A nullable override after a Java to Kotlin conversion 'override' overrides nothing Match the parameter types of the base class
A Kotlin interface constant used from Java cannot find symbol CONSTANT_NAME Write MyInterface.CONSTANT_NAME
A top-level Kotlin function used from Java cannot find symbol myFunction Import it from MyFileKt
object : JavaInterface() This type does not have a constructor Remove the parentheses

Examples

  • intellij.javascript.regexp (Pattern A): JSRegexpInjector, JSRegexpHost and JSRegExpModifierProvider moved out of javascript-backend.
  • intellij.javascript.backend.css (Pattern B): the JsCssIntegrationHelper extension point in javascript-backend. The users in javascript-ultimate, jsf-core and webpack needed fixes.
  • intellij.javascript.backend.spellchecker (Pattern A): CoffeeScript subclasses JSSpellcheckingStrategy, so the module is public, and the class and its inner tokenizer are open.
  • intellij.javascript.backend.xml (Pattern A and B): about 40 files moved, and the JsXmlContextHelper extension point replaced the XmlTag checks in about 60 files.
  • intellij.vuejs.backend.css (Pattern B, three extension points): VueCssExtractHelper passes a List<CssSelectorSuffix> as Any? state. VueCssLanguageProvider returns Language, not PostCssLanguage, to stop a supertype chain.

A content module goes to lib/<module-name .jar when it is embedded, and to lib/modules/<module-name .jar in the other cases. When the layout spec becomes empty, remove the whole pluginAuto or plugin call. 4. Keep compatibility with external plugins Skip this step for loading="embedded" . Call the get external usage statistics tool for each public class. The index covers only Marketplace plugins, so an empty result does not prove safety. If there are external usages, call find external usages on plugin.xml to see how the external plugins depend on the plugin. Then do the common steps. Extract an optional dependency Use this to make a dependency X of a host module optional: move the code that uses X into a new content module. The host module works when the new module is absent, and behaves the same when it is present. Choose the pattern - Pattern A, a simple move. The code that uses X is in a few files, and the host module does not call them. Move these files to the new module. - Pattern B, an extension point. The core files of the host module refer to X in many places. Declare an extension point in the host module without X imports. Implement it in the new module, and replace each direct X call with a null-safe static helper. 1. Create the module Create the module with bun build/jps-module.mjs create <module-dir /<module-name .iml --plugin <plugin.xml . The kind is usually empty , which makes it optional . Add its dependencies with the module-dependencies skill: the host module and X. 2. Move the code - Keep the type of a moved file, Kotlin or Java. Write new code in Kotlin. - Move the file and change its package declaration together. - Keep the availability in IDEA Free mode. The host module and the new module both keep the availability of the original module. PluginsAvailableInIdeaFreeModeTest checks this. Bazel strict deps needs a direct .iml dependency for each class that the code uses. These classes live in modules that their package names do not suggest: Class(es) Package .iml module Bazel target ----------- --------- --------------- -------------- ExecutionException , GeneralCommandLine , KillableColoredProcessHandler , OSProcessHandler , ScriptRunnerUtil , Url , NetUtils com.intellij.execution. , com.intellij.util. intellij.platform.ide.util.io @community//platform/platform-util-io:ide-util-io AsyncPromise , Promise org.jetbrains.concurrency intellij.platform.concurrency @community//platform/util/concurrency AppExecutorUtil , ProcessAdapter , ProcessEvent , ProcessOutputTypes , ParametersListUtil , FileUtil , StringUtil com.intellij.util. , com.intellij.openapi.util. intellij.platform.util @community//platform/util Editor com.intellij.openapi.editor intellij.platform.editor.ui @community//platform/editor-ui-api MultipleLangCommentProvider com.intellij.psi.templateLanguages intellij.platform.lang.impl @community//platform/lang-impl When the code calls a method whose return type comes from a third module, that module is also a direct dependency. Kotlin checks the return type at compile time. 3. Declare the extension point (Pattern B only) Declare the extension point in the descriptor of the host module with qualifiedName : xml <extensionPoints <extensionPoint qualifiedName="com.intellij.<language .<epName " interface="com.intellij.<language .<feature .MyFeatureHelper" dynamic="true"/ </extensionPoints Write the interface in the host module, without X imports. Give it @JvmStatic helpers that return a no-op result when no extension is registered: kotlin interface MyFeatureHelper { fun doSomething(element: PsiElement): Boolean companion object { @JvmField val EP = ExtensionPointName.create<MyFeatureHelper ("com.intellij.<language .<epName ") // An extension point can have several extensions. Process all of them. @JvmStatic fun checkSomething(element: PsiElement?): Boolean = element != null && EP.extensionList.any { it.doSomething(element) } } } Register the implementation in the descriptor of the new module: xml <extensions defaultExtensionNs="com.intellij" <<language .<epName implementation="com.intellij.<language .<feature .MyFeatureHelperImpl"/ </extensions When the operations of X form a lifecycle, put them in one extension point, not one per method. When a step passes state of an X type to a later step, type the state as Any? in the interface. The implementation casts it back: kotlin // In the host module, without X imports interface MyLifecycleHelper { fun captureState(file: PsiFile): Any? fun applyState(file: PsiFile, state: Any?) } // In the new module internal class MyLifecycleHelperImpl : MyLifecycleHelper { override fun captureState(file: PsiFile): Any? = getThings(file) override fun applyState(file: PsiFile, state: Any?) { @Suppress("UNCHECKED CAST") val things = state as? List<XThing ?: emptyList() } } 4. Fix the users of the removed dependency A module that used X through the host module can break. AllProductsPackagingTest targetValidations names it. Add the dependency to its descriptor before the <!-- region Generated dependencies -- marker, inside the same <dependencies tag: xml <dependencies <module name="intellij.some.formerly.transitive.module"/ <!-- region Generated dependencies - run Generate Product Layouts to regenerate -- ... <!-- endregion -- </dependencies Do not add a second <dependencies tag. AllProductsPackagingTest suiteValidations then reports the file as out of sync. When another plugin uses a moved class, do these steps for that plugin: 1. Add <module name="intellij.new.module"/ to its descriptor. 2. Add the module to its .iml with the module-dependencies skill. 3. Set the visibility of the new module. The docs say which level to use. Kotlin classes are final by default. When another module subclasses a moved class or its inner class, mark both classes open . Otherwise the other module fails with cannot inherit from final class . Then do the common steps. Common steps 1. Run ./build/jpsModelToBazel.cmd after an .iml change. In a community checkout, run ./build/jpsModelToBazelCommunityOnly.cmd . 2. Run ./bazel.cmd run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool . It generates the <dependencies of the module descriptors from the .iml files. Read each change that it makes. 3. Run ./community/tools/bt.cmd build for the new module and for each module whose descriptor changed. 4. Run the tests. bt refuses intellij.projectStructureTests , because its tests do not run under Bazel yet, so these tests use tests.cmd . Run the tests.cmd runs one at a time. Each run stops the ide-tests processes of a run that is still in progress. bash ./community/tools/bt.cmd //build/tests/smoke:all-products-packaging test ./tests.cmd --module intellij.projectStructureTests --test com.intellij.ideaProjectStructure.fast.IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest ./tests.cmd --module intellij.projectStructureTests --test com.intellij.ideaProjectStructure.fast.PluginsAvailableInIdeaFreeModeTest For Rider, also run ./tests.cmd --module intellij.rider.build.tests --test com.jetbrains.rider.build.RiderPackagingTest from the ultimate root. After a conversion, search for the old descriptor file name. No xi:include or config-file reference to it can remain. Pitfalls Pitfall Symptom Fix --------- --------- ----- A src tree that repeats the root package as directories Deep src/com/intellij/... folders Keep the package prefix of src , and move the files up A package outside com.<module-name IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest fails Rename the package. Do not add an entry to non-standard-root-packages.txt for a new module A moved file with the old package declaration IntelliJProjectPackageNamesTest : "packages [com.old.pkg] are found in the module" Change the package declaration with the move An extension point with name instead of qualifiedName The extension point is not found Use qualifiedName="com.intellij.<language .<epName " A skipped plugin-model-tool run The generated descriptors have stale dependencies Run ./bazel.cmd run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool A supertype in a removed dependency Cannot access 'com.X.BaseClass' which is a supertype of 'SubClass' Kotlin needs the full supertype chain of each used type. Move the use of SubClass into the extension point implementation, and return a type without X A template dependency with scope="RUNTIME" Cannot access built-in declaration 'kotlin.Any' , or an unresolved class of the .shared module Change the scope of kotlin-stdlib or of the .shared module to compile A class hierarchy that needs a platform dependency cannot access BaseClass: class file not found Keep the platform dependency, also without direct imports A large move Many modules fail to compile After you move 10 or more files, build //plugins/... //contrib/... A nullable override after a Java to Kotlin conversion 'override' overrides nothing Match the parameter types of the base class A Kotlin interface constant used from Java cannot find symbol CONSTANT NAME Write MyInterface.CONSTANT NAME A top-level Kotlin function used from Java cannot find symbol myFunction Import it from MyFileKt object : JavaInterface() This type does not have a constructor Remove the parentheses Examples - intellij.javascript.regexp (Pattern A): JSRegexpInjector , JSRegexpHost and JSRegExpModifierProvider moved out of javascript-backend . - intellij.javascript.backend.css (Pattern B): the JsCssIntegrationHelper extension point in javascript-backend . The users in javascript-ultimate , jsf-core and webpack needed fixes. - intellij.javascript.backend.spellchecker (Pattern A): CoffeeScript subclasses JSSpellcheckingStrategy , so the module is public , and the class and its inner tokenizer are open . - intellij.javascript.backend.xml (Pattern A and B): about 40 files moved, and the JsXmlContextHelper extension point replaced the XmlTag checks in about 60 files. - intellij.vuejs.backend.css (Pattern B, three extension points): VueCssExtractHelper passes a List<CssSelectorSuffix as Any? state. VueCssLanguageProvider returns Language , not PostCssLanguage , to stop a supertype chain.

skills.name: debugging
skills.description: Debug IntelliJ IDE failures.
skills.html:
Debugging

Documentation

  • Logger FAQ
  • How to Investigate Freezes
  • Exception Analyzing FAQ

Searching idea.log

Log Levels:

  • FINE = debug level (from LOG.debug { })
  • INFO = info level (from LOG.info())

Category Format: #<abbreviated.package.path>.<ClassName> for a class under com.intellij, com.jetbrains or org.jetbrains. The package path of another class stays in full.

Example: com.intellij.openapi.wm.impl.status.IdeStatusBarImpl → #c.i.o.w.i.s.IdeStatusBarImpl

Search Example:

# Debug logs from IdeStatusBarImpl
grep "FINE - #c.i.o.w.i.s.IdeStatusBarImpl" idea.log

skills.name: driver-ui-tests
skills.description: Write IntelliJ UI tests with IDE Starter or UI Driver, or run one off-screen to verify a change.
skills.html:
Driver UI Tests Guide

Three files sit next to this one. Read find-elements.md when you look for a component or read the IDE state. Read api.md when you need the call for an action, a wait or a startup flag. Read debug.md when a test fails.

Critical Rules

  • Never use Thread.sleep() or delay() - Driver framework automatically waits for UI elements
  • Wrap test logic in step("description") { } for better logs
  • Verify assertions actually fail – Comment out the action being tested and confirm the test fails. If it still passes, your assertion is too weak.
  • Use common UI components – create new if necessary
  • Keep a helper for a specific test scenario private – keep it in its test class. Put a reusable helper into a common UI component
  • Do not add retries to test-sdk – a retry hides the cause of a failure. Find the cause and wait for the correct UI state. If a test really needs withRetries, keep it in the test module
  • Do not write a workaround for a bug – when the cause is a defect of the product, of the test framework or of the Driver API, file an issue in the AT project of YouTrack, and link it from the test. Use the youtrack skill. A workaround, such as a sleep, a second attempt, a try/catch or a weaker assertion, hides the defect and keeps the test green over broken behavior

Where to look

A test uses JUnit 6 with the IDE Starter framework and the UI Driver framework:

What you need Where it is
The Driver framework community/platform/remote-driver
Common UI components community/platform/remote-driver/test-sdk/src/com/intellij/driver/sdk/ui
UI test examples tests/remote-driver-tests
Runnable examples of each rule here tests/intellij.ide.starter.extended/tests/com/intellij/ide/starter/extended/docexamples
The test case of a project, a com.intellij.ide.starter.models.TestCase a *Cases.kt or a *CachedProjects.kt of the product, such as tests/intellij.ide.starter.extended.idea.ultimate/src/com/intellij/ide/starter/extended/idea/ultimate/CachedProjects.kt
The IDE a test runs against the *ProductInit.kt of the product, such as community/tools/intellij.tools.ide.starter.product.idea.ultimate/src/com/intellij/tools/ide/starter/product/idea/ultimate/IdeaUltimateProductInit.kt
The annotations of a test tests/intellij.ide.starter.allure.annotations/src/com/intellij/ide/starter/extended/allure/Annotations.kt

Required Annotations

Every UI test must have the following annotations at the class level:

Annotation Purpose TestOps Custom Field
@Subsystems.* Categorizes the test by subsystem Subsystem
@Features.* Specifies the feature being tested Feature
@Components.* Identifies the component under test Component

For tests linked to TestOps test cases, also add @AllureId("test_case_id") on the test method. The annotation values should match the corresponding TestOps custom fields (Subsystem, Feature, Component).

Test Structure

Write one call chain from the context to useDriverAndCloseIde. Do not keep the context in a variable, and do not keep a BackgroundRun or a Driver in a field. A kept context invites a second launch over project files that no call rewound. A local val run = ...runIdeWithDriver() is correct when the test calls run.restart(), because restart() needs that run.

pauseOnIndicators waits for the indicators before each Driver call, so it also prevents a failure in the middle of the test. Pass it to runIdeWithDriver, and write no waitForIndicators in the test.

@Subsystems.Java
@Features.Completion
@Components.Editor
class MyTest {

    @Test
    @AllureId("123456")  // Required if test case exists in TestOps
    fun `my test name`() {
        Starter.newContext(ideInfo = IdeInfo.IdeaUltimate) { project = myProject }
            .applyVMOptionsPatch {
                addSystemProperty("ide.ui.non.modal.settings.window", "true")
            }
            .runIdeWithDriver(pauseOnIndicators = 5.minutes)
            .useDriverAndCloseIde {
                ideFrame {
                    openFile("src/Main.java")

                    step("Step description") {
                        // Test actions here
                    }
                }
            }
    }
}

applyVMOptionsPatch is safe here because the context is a fresh one for this test. Never patch a cached or a shared context: the change would reach every test that reuses it.

Two cases need more than the pause:

  • The first call does not wait for a frame. The pause waits only on a project that is already open. A UI search waits up to 15 s for its component, and openFile waits for the project frame, but an action that opens a modal dialog, a call such as singleProject(), and a key press all run at once. Put waitForProjectOpen(Timeouts.M) before such a call, and after the test opens or reopens a project.
  • The pause does not work for the test. Only then call waitForIndicators, and mark the test with @OptIn(ManualWaitForIndicators::class). The compiler warns about each other manual wait.

Running Tests from Terminal

Driver tests require a fully built IDE. The tests.cmd script builds the IDE from sources and runs the tests. Run each local test with USE_DOCKER_CONTAINER=true. The container gives a screen of its own, so the test does not lose the focus to your desktop, and the environment matches the build agent:

USE_DOCKER_CONTAINER=true ./tests.cmd \
  --module intellij.driver.tests.java \
  --test com.intellij.driver.tests.idea.java.navigationTests.FindAndGoToTest

Key parameters:

  • --test - fully qualified test class name (or pattern)
  • --module - the module that holds the test class, such as intellij.driver.tests.java

After the run in the container passes, run the test once without the flag. Some failures come up in one environment only. To keep the focus in that run, use the hidden desktop, see references/hidden-desktop.md.

skills.name: duplicate-and-dead-code
skills.description: Find semantic copies and dead code before a plan or a review.
skills.html:
Duplicate and dead code

Each tool gives candidates, not a proof. Read each candidate before you act on it.

The tools

Tool What it finds Use
jscpd exact, --exit-code 1 a copied text (Type-1) the gate of an area
jscpd --ignore-identifiers --kind renamed a copy with renamed names (Type-2) burn-down
jscpd --similarity 0.9 --kind ast two functions with one syntax tree (Type-3) the copy lint
jscpd --semantic --kind semantic two functions that do one thing (Type-4) the copy lint
jscpd --compare <a>/ <b>/ the functions of <a> with no counterpart in <b> a port or two implementations
accio locate '<question>' --mode semantic, accio context '<task>' the code of a behaviour or a task the owner check
accio trace <Name> --direction callers, accio references <Name> the callers and every use of a name the owner check, dead code
accio unused --scope <dir>/ declarations, bundle keys and image variants used nowhere dead code

Run jscpd only through ./community/tools/jscpd.cmd -c <config>. <config> is the .jscpd.json of the area, for example plugins/air/.jscpd.json. An area without a .jscpd.json runs the commands without -c and has no exact gate. Write each JSON report to a temporary directory of your session. The jscpd_test target of the area runs the gate too, for example //plugins/air:air-duplicate-code_test.

Before a plan: the owner check

Do this for each responsibility that the plan adds: a mapping, a policy, a parser, a cache, a lifecycle step.

  1. accio locate '<a full question about the behaviour>' --mode semantic --scope <area>/. On a miss, ask again in other words.
  2. accio context '<the task in words>' --scope <area>/. Name the task by the nouns of the domain, not by a role word such as "mapper".
  3. accio references <ResultType> --scope <area>/ --no-tests --files. A private function that builds the type is an owner too.
  4. For a V1 or V2 change, find the other version: accio files '<Prefix>V1*', accio files '<Prefix>V2*'.
  5. accio trace <Name> --direction callers for each candidate, then read it. A call site marked ? (:57?) fits more than one overload: read it.
  6. For each owner that the plan extends, read the first guard of its entry point and the body of each gate in that guard. A gate whose body is a literal (fun isFeatureEnabled() = false) makes the owner gated off. A registry key that is off by default makes it gated. accio trace and accio unused can mark an entry point that exits under a gate with a literal body as gated off. Without the mark, they count a gated caller as a use, so only the body of the gate tells.

The plan then has an Existing owners line for each owner, in this form: <owner> — live: <caller path> | gated: <gate> — extend | move | new (<why the owner does not fit>). Do not extend a gated-off owner: move its live parts out, or write new code. When the check finds nothing, the line names the queries.

Before a review: the copy lint

The copy lint is a report, not a gate. Run it after the exact gate of the area passes, when the area has one. Give the touched directories and the directories of their owners: the scan compares only the files under the paths it gets.

./community/tools/jscpd.cmd -c <config> --similarity 0.9 --kind ast --absolute \
  --reporters json --output <temp-dir>/ast <touched-dir>...
./community/tools/jscpd.cmd -c <config> --semantic --semantic-scope same --kind semantic \
  --semantic-same-threshold 0.9 --ignore '**/testSrc/**,**/test/**,**/tests/**,**/testFramework/**' \
  --absolute --reporters json --output <temp-dir>/semantic <touched-dir>...

Then keep the pairs that touch a file of the change. Run this from the repository root:

{ git diff --name-only <base>; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } | sed "s|^|$PWD/|" \
  | jq -R . | jq -s . > <temp-dir>/changed.json
jq -r --slurpfile c <temp-dir>/changed.json '.duplicates[]
  | select(.firstFile.name as $a | .secondFile.name as $b | $c[0] | index($a) or index($b))
  | "\(.similarity) \(.firstFile.name):\(.firstFile.start)-\(.firstFile.end) ~ \(.secondFile.name):\(.secondFile.start)-\(.secondFile.end)"' \
  <temp-dir>/ast/jscpd-report.json <temp-dir>/semantic/jscpd-report.json

Filter the report by file, not by kind. An --kind ast pair has "kind": "similar".

  • Do not use --changed or --baseline-from-ref. Each makes a git worktree of the base revision with 1.4 million files.
  • The first --semantic run on a machine needs --semantic-download (a model of 548 MB). The first run on a directory takes minutes. A later run takes below 1 s.
  • Read each pair at 0.90 or more. Below 0.80, most pairs are two functions of one shape.
  • A pair in one file whose two parts are one line apart is a table, not a copy.
  • A pair that the change did not touch is a lead. Report it and do not fix it.
  • A pair that you keep needs a reason in the review: two sides that no shared module can hold, or a wire DTO and its model.

Dead code

accio unused --scope <dir>/ --limit 1000 gives the candidates. The note of the answer explains each mark, and accio unused --help says what the scan leaves out and cannot see.

  • A (generated) icon field: delete its SVG and generate the icon class again with the icons skill. First search the SVG file name over the whole repository. A SKILL.md can name it as an icon, and then the fix is an icon-robots.txt skip.
  • A (published) candidate is a published API. Keep it unless its owner decides otherwise.
  • An area can keep a guide of the candidates that stay, for example plugins/air/docs/guides/dead-code-guide.md. Read it before the triage, and add each candidate that you keep.

To delete a candidate, prove it with accio locate '<name>' without --scope. Then delete it, the tests that test only it, the imports that only it needed, and the KDoc links to it. Delete a dead key from the English bundle only. The translations under localization/ belong to the localization team. Run the tests of the area, and run accio unused again.

On a miss, ask again in other words. 2. accio context '<the task in words ' --scope <area / . Name the task by the nouns of the domain, not by a role word such as "mapper". 3. accio references <ResultType --scope <area / --no-tests --files . A private function that builds the type is an owner too. 4. For a V1 or V2 change, find the other version: accio files '<Prefix V1 ' , accio files '<Prefix V2 ' . 5. accio trace <Name --direction callers for each candidate, then read it. A call site marked ? ( :57? ) fits more than one overload: read it. 6. For each owner that the plan extends, read the first guard of its entry point and the body of each gate in that guard. A gate whose body is a literal ( fun isFeatureEnabled() = false ) makes the owner gated off. A registry key that is off by default makes it gated. accio trace and accio unused can mark an entry point that exits under a gate with a literal body as gated off . Without the mark, they count a gated caller as a use, so only the body of the gate tells. The plan then has an Existing owners line for each owner, in this form: <owner — live: <caller path gated: <gate — extend move new (<why the owner does not fit ) . Do not extend a gated-off owner: move its live parts out, or write new code. When the check finds nothing, the line names the queries. Before a review: the copy lint The copy lint is a report, not a gate. Run it after the exact gate of the area passes, when the area has one. Give the touched directories and the directories of their owners: the scan compares only the files under the paths it gets. bash ./community/tools/jscpd.cmd -c <config --similarity 0.9 --kind ast --absolute \ --reporters json --output <temp-dir /ast <touched-dir ... ./community/tools/jscpd.cmd -c <config --semantic --semantic-scope same --kind semantic \ --semantic-same-threshold 0.9 --ignore ' /testSrc/ , /test/ , /tests/ , /testFramework/ ' \ --absolute --reporters json --output <temp-dir /semantic <touched-dir ... Then keep the pairs that touch a file of the change. Run this from the repository root: bash { git diff --name-only <base ; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard; } sed "s ^ $PWD/ " \ jq -R . jq -s . <temp-dir /changed.json jq -r --slurpfile c <temp-dir /changed.json '.duplicates[] select(.firstFile.name as $a .secondFile.name as $b $c[0] index($a) or index($b)) "\(.similarity) \(.firstFile.name):\(.firstFile.start)-\(.firstFile.end) \(.secondFile.name):\(.secondFile.start)-\(.secondFile.end)"' \ <temp-dir /ast/jscpd-report.json <temp-dir /semantic/jscpd-report.json Filter the report by file, not by kind . An --kind ast pair has "kind": "similar" . - Do not use --changed or --baseline-from-ref . Each makes a git worktree of the base revision with 1.4 million files. - The first --semantic run on a machine needs --semantic-download (a model of 548 MB). The first run on a directory takes minutes. A later run takes below 1 s. - Read each pair at 0.90 or more. Below 0.80, most pairs are two functions of one shape. - A pair in one file whose two parts are one line apart is a table, not a copy. - A pair that the change did not touch is a lead. Report it and do not fix it. - A pair that you keep needs a reason in the review: two sides that no shared module can hold, or a wire DTO and its model. Dead code accio unused --scope <dir / --limit 1000 gives the candidates. The note of the answer explains each mark, and accio unused --help says what the scan leaves out and cannot see. - A (generated) icon field: delete its SVG and generate the icon class again with the icons skill. First search the SVG file name over the whole repository. A SKILL.md can name it as an icon, and then the fix is an icon-robots.txt skip. - A (published) candidate is a published API. Keep it unless its owner decides otherwise. - An area can keep a guide of the candidates that stay, for example plugins/air/docs/guides/dead-code-guide.md . Read it before the triage, and add each candidate that you keep. To delete a candidate, prove it with accio locate '<name ' without --scope . Then delete it, the tests that test only it, the imports that only it needed, and the KDoc links to it. Delete a dead key from the English bundle only. The translations under localization/ belong to the localization team. Run the tests of the area, and run accio unused again.

skills.name: eel
skills.description: Use IntelliJ EEL APIs for process execution, paths, WSL, or Docker.
skills.html:
Eel Skill

Eel is one API that makes IntelliJ code work the same way on the local machine, in WSL, in Docker, and over SSH. It replaces scattered WSL checks, java.io.File, System.getenv, ProcessBuilder, and SystemInfo with a single abstraction.

Read community/platform/eel/docs/agents/README.md first. It holds the rules, the reading order, and where a new document goes.
